title: Quarter batch (2^17, device batch 64)
description: TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**19 -> 2**17 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 -> 64, so grad_accum stays 1; nothing else changed.
reflection: val_bpb 0.996178 vs baseline 0.997359 (-0.00118). 3211 steps, 420.9M tokens, steady-state MFU 33.78%, peak VRAM 22.7GB (down from the 128-batch baseline). Confirms the batch axis is real but the payoff is small: the smaller device batch costs throughput (MFU 33.8% vs ~39-40% in the flat part of the log, because the Muon+AdamW step now runs once per 131K tokens instead of once per 524K), so only ~420M of the possible ~480M tokens get processed, and the extra steps only just outweigh that. The interesting comparison is against a0/a2's 2^18 runs: if 2^18 beats 2^17 then we have bracketed the optimum at 2^18 and the axis is done; if 2^17 beats 2^18 the optimum is lower still but the MFU cost means going below 2^17 is unlikely to pay. Either way this axis looks worth ~0.001-0.002 bpb total, i.e. it is not where the remaining headroom is -- model shape (depth 8 / dim 512 is thin) and schedule are untouched and should get the next slots.
